item.content:encoded:
The Carter Center Educational Programs offer students and recent graduates opportunities to gain practical professional experience while contributing to initiatives focused on peace, health and organizational operations. The programs are designed to help emerging professionals develop career-relevant skills, explore potential career pathways and contribute to the Carter Center’s mission of advancing peace and health around the world.

For more than four decades, the Carter Center’s Educational Programs have supported the professional development of thousands of interns and graduate assistants. According to the Center, nearly 4,000 interns and graduate assistants from around the world have participated in its educational programs, gaining experience while contributing to the organization’s work.

The current opportunities include internships for undergraduate students, graduate students and recent graduates, as well as funded graduate assistantships for currently enrolled master’s and doctoral students.

About The Carter Center Educational Programs

The Carter Center is an organization whose work focuses substantially on promoting peace, improving health and addressing global challenges. Its Educational Programs provide students and early-career professionals with opportunities to gain exposure to this work in a professional environment.

The programs are intended not only to provide participants with work experience, but also to help develop a new generation of professionals interested in contributing to peace, health and related fields.

Participants can potentially gain experience through program areas including:

  • Peace
  • Health
  • Operations
  • Research and program support
  • Professional and organizational activities related to the Center’s work

The opportunities can therefore be relevant to students and graduates pursuing a wide range of academic and professional interests.

1. The Carter Center Internship Program

The Carter Center’s internship program provides opportunities for students and recent graduates to develop professional skills, gain practical experience and explore career options connected to their areas of interest.

The program is particularly suited to candidates who can demonstrate strong academic performance alongside academic, professional or personal experiences and interests that relate to the Carter Center’s programs.

Interns are based in Atlanta, United States, making the location an important consideration for prospective applicants.

Who Can Apply for the Internship?

To qualify for the internship program, applicants must fall into one of the following categories:

  • Undergraduate juniors
  • Undergraduate seniors
  • Graduate students
  • Recent graduates

For recent graduates, the applicant must have graduated within the previous 24 months.

This means that the program is aimed primarily at students who are relatively advanced in their undergraduate studies, individuals undertaking graduate-level education, and people who have recently completed their degrees.

What Makes a Strong Internship Candidate?

The Carter Center indicates that strong candidates demonstrate superior academic ability and have relevant academic, professional or personal experience and interests connected to the Center’s programs.

Applicants can therefore strengthen their applications by clearly demonstrating how their:

  • Academic background
  • Previous professional experience
  • Research interests
  • Volunteer activities
  • Leadership experience
  • Communication skills
  • International or community engagement
  • Career aspirations

relate to the work of the Carter Center.

Rather than simply presenting academic qualifications, prospective applicants should demonstrate a clear connection between their background and the type of work carried out by the organization.

Internship Program Areas

The Carter Center identifies three broad areas in which internship opportunities may be available:

Peace

Internship opportunities connected to the Peace program can be relevant to individuals interested in areas such as international peacebuilding, conflict prevention, diplomacy, human rights, governance and related global affairs.

Students with academic backgrounds in international relations, political science, diplomacy, development studies, peace and conflict studies, law, communications and related disciplines may find relevant opportunities depending on the positions available during a particular application cycle.

Health

The Health program provides opportunities associated with the Carter Center’s global health work.

Potentially relevant backgrounds may include public health, global health, health communications, development studies, epidemiology, social sciences and other disciplines related to international health and development.

The precise academic or professional requirements will depend on the individual internship opportunity.

Operations

The Operations area encompasses work supporting the effective functioning of the organization.

Opportunities in this area may be relevant to students and graduates interested in areas such as administration, communications, finance, human resources, information management, project support and other organizational functions, depending on the available positions.

Applicants should always review the specific requirements of individual opportunities before applying.

Internship Location

An important consideration for international applicants is that the Carter Center states that its internship opportunities are based in Atlanta.

Therefore, while the Educational Programs have an international orientation and the Center has welcomed participants from around the world, applicants should not assume that the internships are remote.

Prospective applicants should carefully review the individual internship announcement for information concerning location, working arrangements and any additional requirements.

2. Carter Center Graduate Assistantship Program

In addition to internships, the Carter Center offers a Graduate Assistantship Program for a limited number of graduate students.

Unlike the internship program, the graduate assistantship is specifically designed for currently enrolled master’s and doctoral students.

The assistantships provide funded opportunities and require a substantial commitment from successful participants.

Graduate Assistantship Commitment

Graduate assistants are required to make a:

  • 9–12 month commitment
  • 20-hour-per-week commitment

The program therefore represents a significant professional and academic commitment rather than a short-term placement.

Graduate assistants receive hourly compensation for their work.

The opportunities are also based in Atlanta, meaning applicants should take the location and associated practical arrangements into account when considering the program.

Who Is Eligible for the Graduate Assistantship?

The Graduate Assistantship Program is intended for students who are currently enrolled in master’s or doctoral degree programs.

This distinction is important because the graduate assistantship is not simply an extension of the undergraduate internship program.

Applicants should be actively pursuing graduate-level studies and should review the requirements of the specific assistantship opportunity for any additional eligibility conditions.

Graduate Assistantship Program Areas

Graduate assistantship opportunities may be available across three broad areas:

Peace

Graduate students interested in peace, conflict resolution, international affairs, governance, diplomacy, human rights and related disciplines may find opportunities within the Peace program, depending on the positions available.

Health

Students pursuing graduate-level studies related to public health, global health, international development and other relevant disciplines may find opportunities within the Health program.

Operations

Graduate assistantships in Operations may be relevant to students with interests and qualifications in areas that support organizational management and administration.

The actual responsibilities and educational requirements can vary by position, so applicants should examine each available opportunity individually.

2027 Carter Center Internship Deadlines

The Carter Center has announced application deadlines for three internship sessions in 2027.

Spring 2027 Internship

  • Application deadline: October 12, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET
  • Start date: January 12, 2027

Applicants interested in the Spring 2027 session should ensure that their applications are submitted before the stated deadline.

Summer 2027 Internship

  • Application deadline: March 1, 2027, at 11:59 p.m. ET
  • Start date: May 18, 2027

The Summer session may be particularly relevant to students whose academic calendars allow them to undertake professional placements during this period.

Fall 2027 Internship

  • Application deadline: June 14, 2027, at 11:59 p.m. ET
  • Start date: August 27, 2027

Applicants seeking an internship beginning in the Fall 2027 session should plan their applications around the June deadline.

2027 Carter Center Graduate Assistantship Deadline

The Graduate Assistantship application cycle has a separate timeline.

According to the Carter Center:

  • Application opens: February 2027
  • Application deadline: April 23, 2027, at 11:59 p.m. ET
  • Recommendation letters deadline: April 30, 2027, at 11:59 p.m. ET

The recommendation-letter deadline is later than the main application deadline, but applicants should not wait until the final days to arrange their references.

Because recommendation letters are an important part of many graduate-level applications, prospective applicants should identify suitable referees well before the application deadline.

What Participants Can Gain from the Program

The Carter Center Educational Programs can provide participants with several forms of professional and academic development.

1. Practical Professional Experience

Participants have the opportunity to gain hands-on experience within an established organization working on international peace and health issues.

This can help bridge the gap between academic study and professional employment.

2. Exposure to Peace and Health Work

The program allows participants to gain exposure to the practical application of concepts related to peace, health and organizational operations.

For students interested in international development, global affairs, public health, diplomacy and related areas, this type of experience can provide valuable insight into professional environments.

3. Career Exploration

The internship program is explicitly designed to help students and recent graduates explore career options in their fields.

This can be particularly useful for candidates who are still determining which professional pathway they want to pursue.

4. Development of Professional Skills

Participants can develop practical workplace skills that complement their academic qualifications.

Depending on the specific position, these may include:

  • Research
  • Writing
  • Communication
  • Project support
  • Program coordination
  • Data-related work
  • Administrative skills
  • Team collaboration
  • Professional correspondence
  • Organizational skills
  • Problem-solving

The exact skills developed will depend on the specific role and program area.

5. Exposure to an Internationally Oriented Organization

The Carter Center’s programs are connected to international peace and health initiatives, providing participants with an opportunity to understand how a major organization approaches complex global challenges.

This exposure can be valuable for individuals planning careers in international organizations, nongovernmental organizations, government institutions, development agencies, research institutions and related sectors.

Qualifications and Backgrounds That May Be Relevant

The Carter Center does not present one universal academic discipline for every internship or graduate assistantship. Instead, requirements can vary according to the specific position.

However, the programs may be relevant to applicants with backgrounds connected to areas such as:

  • International relations
  • Diplomacy
  • Political science
  • Peace and conflict studies
  • Development studies
  • Public policy
  • Public health
  • Global health
  • International development
  • Communications
  • Journalism
  • Social sciences
  • Research
  • Administration
  • Business and management
  • Finance
  • Human resources
  • Operations
  • Data and information management
  • Other disciplines relevant to individual program positions

Applicants should not assume that studying one of these fields automatically guarantees eligibility. The specific internship or assistantship description should be used to determine whether an applicant’s academic and professional background matches the position.

International Applicants and Countries Eligible to Apply

The Carter Center states that its Educational Programs have provided opportunities to interns and graduate assistants from around the world.

This indicates that the programs have an international participant base. However, the information provided on the program page does not establish a blanket rule that every internship or graduate assistantship is open to nationals of every country without additional conditions.

International applicants should therefore check:

  • The eligibility requirements of the specific position
  • Whether international students are eligible
  • Any requirements relating to study status
  • U.S. work authorization requirements, where applicable
  • Whether the position has additional location or documentation requirements
  • Any other conditions included in the individual vacancy announcement

The programs are physically based in Atlanta, United States, which is particularly important for applicants currently living outside the U.S.

Race, Nationality and Continent Eligibility

The Carter Center’s description emphasizes that its Educational Programs have included participants from around the world. The information supplied for these opportunities does not identify a specific race, ethnicity or continent as a prerequisite for applying.

Accordingly, eligibility should be determined primarily from the formal requirements of the specific opportunity rather than assuming that the program is restricted to applicants from a particular racial, national or continental group.

International applicants, including prospective applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Oceania and other regions, should consult the detailed application requirements for the particular position to determine whether they meet all applicable conditions.

For applicants from Kenya and elsewhere in Africa, the Atlanta-based nature of the program and any U.S. eligibility or authorization requirements should be examined carefully before applying.

How to Prepare a Strong Carter Center Application

Prospective applicants can take several practical steps to prepare for these opportunities.

1. Identify the Right Program

First determine whether you are applying for:

  • An undergraduate or recent graduate internship, or
  • A graduate assistantship for a master’s or doctoral program.

The eligibility requirements differ between these two pathways.

2. Review the Specific Program Area

Consider whether your background aligns with:

  • Peace
  • Health
  • Operations

Your application should make the connection between your experience and the relevant program area clear.

3. Demonstrate Academic Strength

Because the Carter Center identifies superior academic ability as a characteristic of strong internship candidates, applicants should ensure that their academic achievements are clearly presented.

This could include relevant degrees, academic projects, research, awards or other evidence of academic engagement.

4. Highlight Relevant Experience

Do not focus exclusively on academic qualifications.

Relevant experience can include:

  • Internships
  • Employment
  • Research projects
  • Volunteer activities
  • Leadership roles
  • Community engagement
  • Student organizations
  • Professional projects

The strongest examples are those that demonstrate skills or interests relevant to the Carter Center’s work.

5. Connect Your Career Goals to the Opportunity

Applicants should explain why the particular program fits into their professional development.

For example, a candidate interested in international peacebuilding could explain how an internship in the Peace program would complement their academic training and career interests.

Similarly, a public health graduate student could demonstrate how a Health assistantship aligns with their research and professional objectives.

6. Prepare Early

Applicants should pay close attention to the deadlines because the internship program has different deadlines for Spring, Summer and Fall sessions.

Graduate assistantship applicants should also remember that recommendation letters have a separate deadline.

Preparing application materials and contacting referees early can reduce the risk of missing a deadline.

APPLY HERE

Key Dates at a Glance

Opportunity Application Deadline Start/Application Timing
Spring 2027 Internship October 12, 2026, 11:59 p.m. ET Starts January 12, 2027
Summer 2027 Internship March 1, 2027, 11:59 p.m. ET Starts May 18, 2027
Fall 2027 Internship June 14, 2027, 11:59 p.m. ET Starts August 27, 2027
Graduate Assistantship April 23, 2027, 11:59 p.m. ET Application opens February 2027
Graduate Assistantship Recommendation Letters April 30, 2027, 11:59 p.m. ET —

All times listed above are Eastern Time (ET).

Why This Opportunity May Be Relevant to Students and Recent Graduates

The Carter Center Educational Programs combine academic development with practical exposure to work related to peace, health and organizational operations.

For undergraduate juniors and seniors, the internship program can provide an opportunity to gain professional experience before graduation. For recent graduates, it can offer a pathway for gaining additional experience during the early stages of their careers.

For master’s and doctoral students, the Graduate Assistantship Program provides a longer-term opportunity involving a 9–12 month commitment and 20 hours of work per week, together with hourly compensation.

The programs can therefore serve different stages of academic and professional development.

Important Considerations Before Applying

Applicants should keep several factors in mind.

Location: The internships and graduate assistantships are based in Atlanta, rather than being presented as remote opportunities.

Academic status: Internship applicants must be undergraduate juniors or seniors, graduate students or recent graduates within the previous 24 months. Graduate assistantship applicants must be currently enrolled in master’s or doctoral programs.

Program fit: Candidates should demonstrate relevant academic, professional or personal interests connected to Carter Center programs.

Timing: Each internship session has a different deadline, while graduate assistantships have a separate application and recommendation-letter schedule.

International eligibility: The Center has welcomed participants from around the world, but applicants outside the United States should check the requirements associated with the specific opportunity and any applicable U.S. authorization requirements.

Position-specific requirements: Eligibility and responsibilities can differ depending on the individual internship or assistantship, so applicants should read the full description before submitting an application.

Application and Official Information

Prospective applicants should use the Carter Center’s official Educational Programs page to review available opportunities, program requirements, application information, FAQs and current deadlines.

Applicants should also check the official page for updates because individual opportunities and requirements may change between application cycles.

Visit HERE for more information about the Carter Center Educational Programs 2027.

Conclusion

The Carter Center Educational Programs 2027 provide opportunities for students, graduate researchers and recent graduates to gain practical professional experience while contributing to work connected to peace, health and operations.

The internship program is open to eligible undergraduate juniors and seniors, graduate students and recent graduates who completed their studies within the previous 24 months. Meanwhile, the Graduate Assistantship Program provides a limited number of funded opportunities for currently enrolled master’s and doctoral students, with a 9–12 month, 20-hour-per-week commitment and hourly compensation.

With internship sessions beginning in January, May and August 2027, prospective applicants have several entry points throughout the year. The most immediate internship deadline is October 12, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET, for the Spring 2027 session.

Because the opportunities are based in Atlanta and individual positions can have different requirements, applicants should carefully verify eligibility, location, academic requirements and any applicable authorization conditions before applying. Preparing application materials early and demonstrating a clear connection between one’s academic background, experience, career goals and the Carter Center’s work can help ensure that the application accurately reflects the candidate’s qualifications.

item.content:encoded:
The Electoral Integrity Project (EIP) Fellowship Programme 2027 is inviting applications from academics, students, researchers and practitioners interested in conducting research on electoral integrity and strengthening understanding of electoral processes.

The annual Fellowship Programme is designed to bring together researchers and practitioners at different stages of their careers to engage in electoral integrity research with support from the Electoral Integrity Project, fellow participants and members of its International Advisory Board.

The programme provides an opportunity for participants to develop an academic research project, produce a working paper, present their research at the EIP’s annual workshop and participate in monthly seminars where Fellows can receive feedback and engage in discussion with other researchers and practitioners.

The 2027 Electoral Integrity Project Fellowship Programme application deadline is 30 October 2026.

About the Electoral Integrity Project Fellowship

The Electoral Integrity Project Fellowship is structured around research and professional engagement in the field of electoral integrity.

Rather than being limited to one academic career stage, the programme includes different Fellowship categories designed for:

  • Master’s students
  • Doctoral students and candidates
  • Postdoctoral researchers
  • Assistant Professors
  • Lecturers
  • Associate Professors
  • Full Professors
  • Senior and Principal Lecturers
  • Readers and equivalent academic positions
  • Practitioners working in fields connected to electoral integrity

This structure allows researchers at different stages of their careers to participate in a common research environment while developing work related to the quality, credibility and functioning of electoral processes.

The programme also includes named fellowships that provide additional funding opportunities for specific groups and research themes.

What Is Electoral Integrity?

Electoral integrity broadly concerns the quality and credibility of electoral processes and the conditions under which elections are conducted.

Research in this area can involve a wide range of questions concerning elections, electoral institutions, political participation, electoral management, democratic processes and the factors that influence the functioning of elections.

The Fellowship therefore provides a research environment for scholars and practitioners whose work contributes to understanding electoral integrity from academic, institutional, policy or professional perspectives.

Because the programme is open to different types of researchers and practitioners, projects can potentially approach electoral integrity from multiple disciplinary and professional angles.

What Does the Fellowship Programme Offer?

The Electoral Integrity Project Fellowship has several core components designed to help Fellows develop and communicate their research.

1. Conduct an Academic Research Project

Fellows are expected to conduct an academic research project on a topic related to electoral integrity.

This provides participants with an opportunity to develop a focused research agenda while engaging with the broader work of the Electoral Integrity Project.

The research project can become an important foundation for further academic or professional work, particularly for students and early-career researchers developing their expertise in electoral studies.

2. Produce a Working Paper

Fellows are expected to produce a working paper based on their research project.

A working paper provides an opportunity to develop research findings into a structured academic document that can be discussed, reviewed and refined.

For Master’s and doctoral researchers, this can also provide useful experience in developing research for academic audiences.

3. Present Research at the Annual Workshop

The Fellowship includes preparation of an associated conference presentation for the EIP’s annual workshop.

This component allows Fellows to communicate their research to other researchers and participants working in electoral integrity and related areas.

Presenting research can also help participants develop their academic communication skills and receive perspectives that may contribute to further development of their project.

4. Participate in Monthly Seminars

Fellows participate in monthly seminars where participants present their work.

These seminars are designed to provide opportunities for:

  • Research feedback
  • Academic discussion
  • Exchange of ideas
  • Engagement with other Fellows
  • Development of research arguments
  • Discussion of research methods and findings

The seminar structure makes the Fellowship more than an individual research grant or independent research placement. Participants become part of a continuing research environment in which their work can be discussed with others.

5. Mentoring for Junior Fellows

Junior Fellows have the option of being matched with a senior mentor from the Electoral Integrity Project’s International Advisory Board or established practitioner partners.

This mentoring opportunity can be particularly useful for students and early-career researchers who are developing their research interests and professional networks.

Mentorship can provide an additional opportunity to receive guidance as a research project develops.

Types of Electoral Integrity Project Fellowships

The 2027 Fellowship Programme includes several categories of Fellows.

The categories reflect different levels of academic experience and professional involvement in electoral integrity.

Junior Fellows

Junior Fellows are academics at the level of Master’s or doctoral student/candidate.

This category provides an opportunity for students conducting advanced academic work to participate in electoral integrity research.

It may be relevant to:

  • Master’s students researching elections or related subjects
  • PhD students working on electoral integrity
  • Doctoral candidates studying democracy or electoral processes
  • Graduate researchers developing projects related to electoral institutions

Junior Fellows also have the option of being matched with a senior mentor.

Fellows

The standard Fellows category is intended for academics at the level of:

  • Postdoctoral Fellow
  • Assistant Professor
  • Lecturer
  • Equivalent academic positions

This category is suited to researchers who have moved beyond doctoral study and are developing their academic research careers.

Applicants at this stage may already have established research interests in elections, democracy, political institutions or related subjects.

Senior Fellows

Senior Fellows are academics at the level of:

  • Associate Professor
  • Full Professor
  • Senior Lecturer
  • Principal Lecturer
  • Reader
  • Equivalent academic positions

The category recognizes established academics who are conducting research related to electoral integrity.

Senior Fellows can participate in the research community while contributing their experience and scholarship to discussions surrounding electoral integrity.

Practitioner Fellows

The Practitioner Fellowship is designed for practitioners working in a field related to electoral integrity at any stage of their career.

The Electoral Integrity Project states that practitioners may come from:

  • Government
  • Non-governmental organizations
  • Civil society
  • Industry

This category is particularly relevant for professionals whose practical work connects with electoral processes, election administration, governance, democracy, political institutions or related areas.

The practitioner pathway means that the Fellowship is not restricted exclusively to university-based academics.

Learn More HERE

Named Fellowship Opportunities

In addition to the general Fellowship categories, the Electoral Integrity Project lists two named Fellowship opportunities for the 2027 programme.

These provide additional opportunities for applicants working on particular areas of electoral integrity research.

Carter Center Democracy Fellowships

There are two Carter Center Democracy Fellowships available.

Each Fellowship provides:

US$1,000

The named Fellowships are offered in collaboration with The Carter Center.

The opportunity is specifically intended for:

  • Students
  • Scholars

working on any area of electoral integrity research.

One important feature of the Carter Center Democracy Fellowship is its geographic eligibility.

The Electoral Integrity Project states that the fellowships are available to students or scholars from any country. This means that the named fellowship does not impose a restriction to a particular continent or region.

Applicants interested in this Fellowship should nevertheless review the application requirements and ensure that their proposed work fits within the broader focus on electoral integrity research.

Electoral Management Resiliency Fellowships

There are also two Electoral Management Resiliency Fellowships available.

Each provides:

C$1,000

These Fellowships are intended for junior scholars or practitioners working on projects related to building the resilience of electoral management.

The source identifies several areas that can fall within this research theme, including:

  • Legal frameworks
  • Leadership capacity
  • Financial capacity
  • Emerging technologies
  • Opinion shifts concerning electoral management resiliency

The Fellowships are funded in part by the Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council of Canada.

This named Fellowship can therefore be particularly relevant to researchers and practitioners examining how electoral management institutions can become more resilient in the face of institutional, technological, financial or social changes.

Research Areas Relevant to the Fellowship

The programme is centered on electoral integrity research, which can encompass a broad range of academic and professional questions.

Potential areas of relevance may include research concerning:

  • Electoral institutions
  • Electoral management
  • Election administration
  • Democratic processes
  • Political participation
  • Electoral governance
  • Election-related technologies
  • Electoral law and legal frameworks
  • Political communication
  • Misinformation and elections
  • Political behaviour
  • Election observation
  • Electoral disputes
  • Institutional capacity
  • Electoral security
  • Democratic accountability

Applicants should ensure that their proposed research fits the Fellowship’s stated focus on electoral integrity.

The specific examples above should be treated as possible areas of relevance rather than a prescribed list of eligible research topics, because the supplied programme information does not provide an exhaustive research-topic list.

Why the Research Component Matters

One of the defining characteristics of the Fellowship is its emphasis on producing research rather than simply attending an academic programme.

Participants are expected to develop a research project and transform that work into a working paper and conference presentation.

This structure can help researchers move through several stages of academic development:

  1. Developing a research question.
  2. Conducting the research.
  3. Developing a working paper.
  4. Presenting findings.
  5. Receiving feedback.
  6. Refining the research.

For early-career researchers, this can provide a structured environment in which research is discussed throughout the Fellowship period.

For established academics and practitioners, the Fellowship can provide an opportunity to engage with a wider research community working on electoral integrity.

Networking and Academic Engagement

The Fellowship also creates opportunities for participants to interact with other researchers and professionals working on electoral integrity.

Monthly seminars allow Fellows to present their research and participate in discussion.

This type of academic engagement can be useful for:

  • Exchanging research ideas
  • Receiving constructive feedback
  • Identifying new research questions
  • Learning about related research
  • Developing professional relationships
  • Connecting academic research with practical experience

The involvement of the EIP’s International Advisory Board and practitioner partners also creates opportunities for interaction across academic and professional communities.

Mentorship for Emerging Researchers

Junior Fellows have access to an optional mentoring opportunity.

They may be matched with a senior mentor from:

  • The EIP International Advisory Board, or
  • Established practitioner partners.

For students and doctoral researchers, mentorship can provide an additional layer of professional and academic engagement.

A mentor may help an early-career researcher think through aspects of their research project and broader professional development, although the supplied source does not specify the precise structure or frequency of mentoring sessions.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The Fellowship may be relevant to applicants who are developing academic or professional interests in electoral integrity.

Potential applicants include:

  • Master’s students
  • PhD students
  • Doctoral candidates
  • Postdoctoral researchers
  • Assistant Professors
  • University Lecturers
  • Associate Professors
  • Full Professors
  • Senior Lecturers
  • Principal Lecturers
  • Readers
  • Equivalent academic professionals
  • Government practitioners
  • NGO professionals
  • Civil society practitioners
  • Industry professionals working in fields related to electoral integrity

The appropriate Fellowship category depends on the applicant’s career stage and professional background.

Academic Qualifications and Career Stage

The programme does not impose one universal academic qualification across all Fellowship categories.

Instead, eligibility is connected to the applicant’s professional or academic level.

For Junior Fellows

Applicants should be at the level of a Master’s or doctoral student/candidate.

For Fellows

Applicants should be at the level of a:

  • Postdoctoral Fellow
  • Assistant Professor
  • Lecturer
  • Equivalent position

For Senior Fellows

Applicants should be at the level of:

  • Associate Professor
  • Full Professor
  • Senior Lecturer
  • Principal Lecturer
  • Reader
  • Equivalent position

For Practitioner Fellows

Practitioners can apply at any career stage, provided their professional field is related to electoral integrity.

This includes professionals working in government, NGOs, civil society or industry.

Nationality, Race and Geographic Eligibility

The supplied information does not identify a race, ethnicity or continental restriction for the general Fellowship categories.

It also does not state that applicants must come from a particular country or region for the general Fellowship programme.

Therefore, the source should not be interpreted as restricting the general Fellowship to applicants from Europe, Africa, Asia, North America, Latin America, Oceania or any other particular geographic region.

The clearest nationality statement in the supplied information applies to the Carter Center Democracy Fellowships, which are specifically described as being for students or scholars from any country.

For the Electoral Management Resiliency Fellowships, the source identifies the eligible professional group as junior scholars or practitioners working on relevant electoral management resilience projects, but it does not state a specific nationality, race or continental restriction.

Applicants should therefore avoid assuming that a particular nationality is required unless the specific application instructions state otherwise.

Are African Researchers Eligible?

The supplied information does not exclude African researchers.

Because the general Fellowship description does not specify a geographic exclusion and the Carter Center Democracy Fellowships explicitly accept applicants from any country, researchers based in African countries may be eligible, subject to meeting the relevant academic or practitioner criteria and the requirements of the particular Fellowship category.

The same principle applies to researchers from other parts of the world.

Are International Applicants Eligible?

For the general Fellowship categories, the supplied information does not establish a nationality restriction.

The Carter Center Democracy Fellowship is explicitly described as available to students and scholars from any country.

Consequently, international researchers should consider the programme based on their academic or professional category and the fit of their proposed research with electoral integrity, while checking the application form for any additional requirements.

Application Deadline for the 2027 Fellowship

The Electoral Integrity Project states that:

Applications for the 2027 Fellowship Programme are open until 30 October 2026.

Important deadline information

Application deadline: 30 October 2026

Applicants should not wait until the final day to prepare their applications.

Because the Fellowship requires applicants to identify a research project related to electoral integrity, prospective applicants should allow sufficient time to consider their research topic and prepare the required application information.

How to Apply

The Electoral Integrity Project provides an online application route for the 2027 Fellowship Programme.

Applicants should begin by determining which Fellowship category corresponds to their academic or professional status.

Step 1: Identify your Fellowship category

Determine whether you are applying as:

  • Junior Fellow
  • Fellow
  • Senior Fellow
  • Practitioner Fellow

Applicants interested in the named Fellowships should also determine whether their research fits the requirements for the Carter Center Democracy Fellowship or the Electoral Management Resiliency Fellowship.

Step 2: Identify your research topic

The core requirement across the Fellowship programme is engagement with research related to electoral integrity.

Applicants should therefore have a clear idea of the research project they would like to undertake.

Step 3: Consider your research contribution

Think about the specific question your project addresses and how it contributes to understanding electoral integrity.

A clear research focus can help demonstrate the relevance of the proposed project.

Step 4: Review the Fellowship information

Applicants should carefully review the official Fellowship information and application instructions before submitting their application.

Step 5: Submit the application before the deadline

Applications for the 2027 programme must be submitted by:

30 October 2026.

The official application page is provided by the Electoral Integrity Project through its Fellowship Programme page.

APPLY HERE

What Applicants Should Prepare

Although the supplied source does not provide a complete checklist of application documents, prospective applicants should be prepared to clearly communicate their:

  • Academic or professional status
  • Research interests
  • Proposed electoral integrity research project
  • Relevant background in electoral integrity or related fields
  • Career stage
  • Interest in participating in the Fellowship programme

Applicants should use the official application form and instructions to determine the exact information and documentation required.

Examples from Previous Fellowship Cohorts

The Electoral Integrity Project’s previous Fellows demonstrate the breadth of academic and professional backgrounds represented in the programme.

The 2026 cohort includes researchers and practitioners working on subjects such as:

  • Electoral studies
  • Political communication
  • Misinformation
  • Democratization
  • Comparative political institutions
  • Political parties
  • Electoral management
  • Democracy
  • Public policy
  • Election observation
  • Security
  • Governance
  • Political accountability

For example, the supplied information identifies Yoosuf Ali as a Senior Doctoral Fellow whose research interests include election studies, misinformation ecosystems, political communication and electoral behaviour.

The 2026 cohort also includes senior academics such as Svitlana Chernykh, whose research focuses on democratization and comparative political institutions, including elections, parties and constitutions.

Another Fellow, Constanza Sanhueza Petrarca, has research interests involving democracy, elections and representation and has held research positions at institutions including the WZB Berlin Social Science Center, V-Dem Institute and Sciences Po Paris.

The cohort also demonstrates the programme’s practitioner dimension. Sujith Jayasooriya, for example, is identified as a practitioner Fellow with experience in public policy analysis, political economy and work involving multilateral institutions.

Martyna Hoffman is another practitioner Fellow whose experience includes election observation, electoral research and work with the European Union Election Observation Mission in Sri Lanka.

These examples illustrate that the Fellowship community can include researchers and practitioners with different professional backgrounds and different approaches to electoral integrity research.

The Fellowship and Interdisciplinary Research

The range of previous Fellows also illustrates the interdisciplinary character of electoral integrity research.

Electoral integrity can intersect with fields such as:

  • Political science
  • Sociology
  • Economics
  • Public policy
  • International relations
  • Communications
  • Technology studies
  • Governance
  • Security studies
  • Development studies
  • Law
  • Data analysis

This means that researchers do not necessarily need to approach electoral integrity from a single disciplinary perspective.

A research project can potentially examine electoral integrity through institutional, technological, social, political, economic or communication-related questions, provided that it fits the Fellowship’s focus.

Why the Fellowship Can Be Relevant to PhD Students

For doctoral students and candidates, the Junior Fellowship can provide a research-focused environment during an important stage of academic development.

The combination of:

  • Research project development
  • Working paper production
  • Conference presentation
  • Monthly seminars
  • Optional senior mentorship

can support the development and communication of doctoral-level research.

A PhD student studying elections, democracy, political institutions, electoral management, political communication or related issues may find the Fellowship particularly relevant if their work directly engages with electoral integrity.

Why the Fellowship Can Be Relevant to Established Academics

For postdoctoral researchers, lecturers and professors, the programme offers an opportunity to participate in a research community focused specifically on electoral integrity.

The Fellowship categories recognize researchers at different stages, from postdoctoral and lecturer level through senior academic positions.

Established researchers may also contribute perspectives and experience to discussions involving other Fellows while continuing to develop their own research projects.

Why the Practitioner Fellowship Matters

Electoral integrity is not solely an academic subject.

Government institutions, election-related organizations, civil society groups, NGOs and other organizations are involved in the practical functioning and study of electoral processes.

The Practitioner Fellowship recognizes this by allowing professionals working in relevant fields to participate at any career stage.

Practitioners can therefore approach electoral integrity from an applied perspective, drawing on their professional experiences and institutional knowledge.

Named Funding Opportunities

Applicants should pay particular attention to the two named Fellowship opportunities because they offer additional financial support.

Carter Center Democracy Fellowship

  • Number available: 2
  • Award: US$1,000 each
  • Eligible group: Students or scholars
  • Geographic eligibility: Any country
  • Research focus: Any area of electoral integrity research
  • Partner: The Carter Center

Electoral Management Resiliency Fellowship

  • Number available: 2
  • Award: C$1,000 each
  • Eligible group: Junior scholars or practitioners
  • Research focus: Resilience of electoral management
  • Possible themes: Legal frameworks, leadership capacity, financial capacity, emerging technologies and opinion shifts concerning electoral management resilience
  • Funding: Funded in part by Canada’s Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council

Application Strategy

Prospective applicants can improve the clarity of their application by making sure their research idea is directly connected to electoral integrity.

A useful approach is to clearly identify:

  1. The electoral integrity issue being investigated.
  2. The research question or problem.
  3. Why the issue matters.
  4. The applicant’s relevant academic or professional background.
  5. The type of research the applicant proposes to undertake.
  6. How the project fits within the Fellowship’s research environment.

Applicants should also make sure they apply under the Fellowship category that corresponds to their current academic or professional level.

Important Things to Remember

Before submitting an application, prospective Fellows should keep the following points in mind:

  • The programme is specifically focused on electoral integrity research.
  • The Fellowship includes different categories based on career stage.
  • Junior Fellows are Master’s or doctoral students/candidates.
  • Fellows include postdoctoral researchers, Assistant Professors, Lecturers and equivalents.
  • Senior Fellows include Associate and Full Professors and equivalent positions.
  • Practitioner Fellows can be at any career stage if their work relates to electoral integrity.
  • Junior Fellows have an optional senior mentoring opportunity.
  • Fellows are expected to conduct a research project.
  • Fellows produce a working paper.
  • Fellows prepare a conference presentation for the annual workshop.
  • Monthly seminars provide opportunities for research feedback and discussion.
  • Two Carter Center Democracy Fellowships provide US$1,000 each.
  • The Carter Center Democracy Fellowships are open to students or scholars from any country.
  • Two Electoral Management Resiliency Fellowships provide C$1,000 each.
  • Applications for the 2027 programme close on 30 October 2026.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Electoral Integrity Project Fellowship?

It is an annual Fellowship Programme designed for academics and practitioners at different career stages to engage in research related to electoral integrity with support from the EIP, other Fellows and members of its Advisory Board.

What is the deadline for the 2027 Fellowship?

The application deadline is 30 October 2026.

Can Master’s students apply?

Yes. Master’s students are included in the Junior Fellow category.

Can PhD students apply?

Yes. Doctoral students and candidates are included among Junior Fellows.

Can university lecturers apply?

Yes. Lecturers and equivalent academics are included in the Fellows category.

Can professors apply?

Yes. Associate Professors, Full Professors and equivalent senior academics are included in the Senior Fellow category.

Can practitioners apply?

Yes. Practitioner Fellows can be practitioners in fields related to electoral integrity at any career stage, including professionals from government, NGOs, civil society and industry.

Can applicants from any country apply?

The Carter Center Democracy Fellowships are explicitly open to students or scholars from any country. The supplied information does not establish a universal nationality restriction for the general Fellowship categories.

Is there a Fellowship specifically for electoral management resilience?

Yes. Two Electoral Management Resiliency Fellowships are available for junior scholars or practitioners working on projects related to strengthening electoral management resilience.

How much do the named Fellowships provide?

The Carter Center Democracy Fellowships provide US$1,000 each, while the Electoral Management Resiliency Fellowships provide C$1,000 each.

Is mentoring available?

Yes. Junior Fellows have the option of being matched with a senior mentor from the EIP International Advisory Board or established practitioner partners.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Electoral Integrity Project Fellowship 2027.

Official Application

Applications for the 2027 Electoral Integrity Project Fellowship Programme are open until 30 October 2026.

Interested applicants should consult the official Electoral Integrity Project Fellowship information and use the official application route provided by the organization.

The programme’s application page is listed as “Apply now” on the official Fellowship Programme page.

Conclusion

The Electoral Integrity Project Fellowship 2027 provides a research and professional-development opportunity for academics and practitioners interested in understanding electoral integrity and related questions surrounding electoral processes.

One of the programme’s key features is its broad career-stage structure. Master’s and doctoral students can apply as Junior Fellows, while postdoctoral researchers, lecturers and equivalent academics can apply through the Fellows category. More established academics can participate as Senior Fellows, while practitioners working in relevant fields can apply as Practitioner Fellows.

The programme also goes beyond independent research. Fellows are expected to conduct an academic research project, develop a working paper, prepare a conference presentation and participate in monthly seminars where they can present their work and receive feedback. Junior Fellows additionally have the option of receiving mentorship from a senior member of the EIP’s International Advisory Board or an established practitioner partner.

For applicants seeking additional funding opportunities, the programme includes two Carter Center Democracy Fellowships worth US$1,000 each and two Electoral Management Resiliency Fellowships worth C$1,000 each. The Carter Center Fellowships are particularly broad geographically because they are open to students or scholars from any country working on electoral integrity research.

The programme can therefore be relevant to a wide range of researchers and professionals, from graduate students developing their first major research projects to established academics and practitioners with experience in electoral institutions, governance, election observation and related fields.

Applicants interested in participating in the 2027 Electoral Integrity Project Fellowship Programme should carefully review the Fellowship categories and identify the opportunity that corresponds to their academic or professional stage.

Application deadline: 30 October 2026.

Applicants should submit their applications before the deadline through the official Electoral Integrity Project application process.

Discover more global Fellowship, Research and PhD opportunities on OFY.

item.content:encoded:
Carnegie Mellon University Africa (CMU-Africa) is offering a six-course online Certificate in Artificial Intelligence for Africa, designed for learners who want to develop practical artificial intelligence skills and learn how AI can be applied to challenges and opportunities across the African continent.

The certificate program is cost-free for qualified applicants, making it an accessible opportunity for learners interested in developing technical and analytical skills in artificial intelligence without paying tuition for the program.

Applications and recommendations for the new cohort will be accepted from 15 October to 15 November 2026, while the new cohort is scheduled to begin on 17 January 2027.

The program combines AI context and foundational knowledge with practical technical training. Learners will study subjects ranging from the history and development of artificial intelligence to machine learning, Python, mathematical foundations, and applied generative AI.

This makes the program particularly relevant to students and professionals who want to understand both the broader implications of AI in Africa and the technical skills required to develop AI-powered solutions.

About the Certificate in Artificial Intelligence for Africa

The Certificate in Artificial Intelligence for Africa is a six-course online learning program developed by Carnegie Mellon University Africa.

The program focuses on helping learners develop the knowledge, technical skills, and confidence required to work with AI applications relevant to African contexts.

Rather than focusing exclusively on theoretical concepts, the program incorporates hands-on exercises and industry-standard tools.

According to CMU-Africa, learners will develop the ability to:

  • Understand the purpose, capabilities, and limitations of AI tools and techniques;
  • Apply foundational analytical and technical skills to AI-driven solutions in Africa;
  • Develop AI models and solutions using current tools, frameworks, and best practices;
  • Translate real-world challenges into data-driven AI solutions that are relevant, effective, and deployable; and
  • Evaluate the impact of AI solutions using appropriate metrics, validation techniques, and critical thinking.

The program therefore combines conceptual understanding with practical application.

What Makes This AI Program Relevant to Africa?

Artificial intelligence is increasingly being applied across sectors including healthcare, finance, education, agriculture, telecommunications, public services, business, and technology.

However, AI solutions developed for one environment may not automatically address the needs, infrastructure, data realities, or social contexts of another.

The CMU-Africa certificate is specifically designed around AI applications relevant to Africa.

This contextual approach means learners are introduced not only to AI technologies but also to questions about how AI can be developed and applied to real-world challenges within African environments.

For learners interested in contributing to Africa’s growing technology and digital economy, this can provide an opportunity to develop both technical knowledge and an understanding of the regional context in which AI solutions operate.

The Program Is Cost-Free for Qualified Applicants

One of the key features of the opportunity is that the certificate program is cost-free for qualified applicants.

This means eligible learners do not need to pay tuition for participation in the certificate program.

However, applicants should distinguish between the program being cost-free and all possible personal expenses being covered.

The information provided states that the certificate program is cost-free, but it does not state that CMU-Africa provides funding for items such as:

  • Personal computers;
  • Internet costs;
  • Accommodation;
  • Travel;
  • Living expenses; or
  • Other personal expenses.

Learners should therefore review the official program information carefully to understand what is and is not covered.

What Will Learners Study?

The certificate consists of six courses divided into two main tracks:

Perspective and Context Track

The perspective and context component introduces learners to the broader development and application of artificial intelligence.

It includes:

1. Artificial Intelligence – Past, Present and Future

This course provides a broader perspective on artificial intelligence, helping learners understand how AI has developed and how its capabilities and applications continue to evolve.

It provides important context for learners before they move deeper into technical AI concepts.

2. AI and Machine Learning in Africa

This course focuses specifically on artificial intelligence and machine learning within the African context.

It is particularly relevant for learners who want to understand how AI technologies can be applied to African challenges and opportunities.

Technical Track

The technical component provides learners with foundational and applied skills for developing AI solutions.

It includes:

3. Python for AI

Python is widely used in artificial intelligence, machine learning, data analysis, and software development.

This course introduces learners to Python in the context of AI development and provides an important technical foundation for the other courses.

4. Mathematical Foundations of Machine Learning

Machine learning relies on mathematical concepts to represent data, develop models, and understand algorithms.

This course covers mathematical foundations relevant to machine learning and is particularly important given that applicants are expected to have basic knowledge of linear algebra, probability, and statistics before entering the program.

5. Machine Learning Essentials

This course introduces fundamental machine learning concepts and techniques.

Learners can use these foundations to understand how machines learn from data and how machine learning models can be developed for practical applications.

6. Applied Generative AI

Generative artificial intelligence has become an increasingly important area of AI development.

The applied generative AI course focuses on practical applications of this technology, helping learners understand how generative AI can be used to develop solutions and address real-world problems.

How Long Does the Program Take?

The certificate contains six courses, with each course consisting of approximately 14 or 15 lessons.

Each lesson is designed to take qualified learners approximately three hours to complete.

This means each course requires approximately:

45 hours

of learning time.

Across six courses, the overall program therefore represents a substantial learning commitment.

Learners should plan to spend approximately five to six hours per week to complete the courses at the expected pace.

This is an important consideration for applicants who are studying at university or working full-time.

The online structure provides flexibility, but learners still need to allocate consistent weekly time to successfully complete the program.

Is the Certificate University Credit?

No.

The certificate program is not for university credit.

Instead, learners receive digital credentials for their completed coursework.

Participants earn:

  • A digital badge for each course; and
  • A shareable and verifiable certificate after completing all six courses.

These digital credentials can provide learners with a way to demonstrate their participation and completed training to employers, professional networks, or other relevant audiences.

Career Pathways After the Program

The certificate is designed to support learners at different stages of their careers.

According to CMU-Africa, it can support:

  • Early-career learners seeking internships;
  • Early-career learners seeking entry-level positions; and
  • Mid-career technical professionals seeking to strengthen their AI capabilities.

Potential career areas include:

Machine Learning Applications

Learners can develop foundational knowledge relevant to applying machine learning techniques to practical problems.

AI Application Development

The technical coursework can provide foundational skills relevant to developing applications incorporating artificial intelligence.

AI Product Support

AI products require professionals who understand both technology and how AI-enabled products function within real-world environments.

AI Research and Innovation

The program can also provide foundational knowledge for learners interested in AI research and innovation.

Related AI Fields

The skills developed through the program can potentially be relevant to other emerging AI-related roles and areas.

The certificate itself does not guarantee employment, internships, or admission to another academic program. Its purpose is to develop skills and provide a verifiable credential that learners can use as part of their broader professional development.

Who Is the Program Designed For?

The certificate is designed to accommodate a diverse range of learners interested in advancing their careers or developing their artificial intelligence skills.

The university specifically identifies two broad groups.

Undergraduate Students

Undergraduate students interested in technology, AI, data, computing, engineering, or related areas may find the program relevant to their professional development.

The program can help students begin developing AI competencies before entering the workforce or seeking internships.

Working Professionals

Professionals who are adapting to changes in the labour market can also benefit from the program.

The certificate may be relevant to professionals who want to build AI capabilities alongside their existing career experience.

This is particularly important as AI increasingly becomes integrated into different industries and professional functions.

Prerequisites

Although the program is designed for a diverse group of learners, applicants need to meet certain foundational requirements.

Successful candidates must have basic knowledge of:

Linear Algebra

Linear algebra is an important mathematical foundation for machine learning and AI.

Applicants should have basic familiarity with concepts relevant to mathematical and computational modelling.

Probability and Statistics

Probability and statistics are fundamental to understanding data, uncertainty, model performance, and machine learning techniques.

Applicants should therefore have basic knowledge of these areas before beginning the program.

Computer Programming

Because the technical track includes Python for AI and other computational subjects, applicants must have basic programming knowledge.

The program is therefore not intended as a completely beginner-level introduction to computers or programming.

Computer Access

Learners must have access to:

  • A laptop or desktop computer; and
  • A reliable internet connection.

Because the certificate is delivered online, reliable access to the necessary technology is essential for participating in the coursework and completing the lessons.

Is Prior AI Experience Required?

The information provided does not state that applicants must already be AI professionals or have advanced AI expertise.

Instead, the program is intended for a broad range of learners who want to advance their careers or enhance their AI skills.

However, applicants should not interpret this as meaning that no technical foundation is necessary.

The university specifically identifies basic linear algebra, probability and statistics, and computer programming as prerequisites.

Therefore, learners with some foundational technical and mathematical knowledge may be better positioned to follow the technical coursework.

Program Timeline

Applicants should take note of the key dates.

Applications and Recommendations Open

15 October 2026

Applications and recommendations open on 15 October 2026.

Application Deadline

15 November 2026

Applications and recommendations will be accepted until 15 November 2026.

Applicants should submit their applications before the stated deadline rather than waiting until the final day.

New Cohort Begins

17 January 2027

The new cohort is scheduled to begin on 17 January 2027.

This gives successful applicants time between the end of the application period and the beginning of the program.

How to Prepare Before Applying

Applicants can take several steps to prepare for the application period.

1. Review the Prerequisites

Before applying, assess your knowledge of:

  • Linear algebra;
  • Probability;
  • Statistics; and
  • Computer programming.

If you have studied these subjects previously, identify the courses, training, projects, or professional experience that demonstrate your foundation.

2. Make Sure You Have the Required Technology

Because the certificate is online, make sure you have access to a suitable:

  • Laptop or desktop computer; and
  • Reliable internet connection.

This is particularly important because the program includes technical exercises and practical learning.

3. Consider Your Weekly Availability

The university recommends that learners spend approximately five to six hours per week on the program.

Applicants should therefore consider whether they can consistently dedicate this amount of time alongside their existing academic, professional, or personal responsibilities.

4. Connect the Program to Your Career Goals

Before applying, think about why you want to develop AI skills.

For example, your goal might be to:

  • Transition into AI-related work;
  • Strengthen an existing technical career;
  • Prepare for internships;
  • Explore AI product development;
  • Work on technology solutions for African challenges;
  • Develop AI-related entrepreneurial ideas;
  • Expand your data and analytical skills; or
  • Understand how AI can be applied within your existing profession.

Having a clear professional reason for pursuing the certificate can help you approach the program more strategically.

Why the Certificate Could Be Relevant Across Different Industries

Artificial intelligence is not limited to software companies.

AI technologies are increasingly relevant to fields such as:

  • Healthcare;
  • Finance;
  • Education;
  • Agriculture;
  • Marketing;
  • Telecommunications;
  • Manufacturing;
  • Public services;
  • Research;
  • Business operations; and
  • Digital products.

For professionals who already have expertise in another field, developing AI literacy can provide an additional layer of technical knowledge.

For example, a healthcare professional interested in digital health could explore AI applications in healthcare, while a marketing professional could explore AI-enabled customer analytics or generative AI applications.

The CMU-Africa program’s emphasis on real-world AI solutions and the African context may be particularly relevant to learners who want to apply technology to problems within African markets.

Learning From Carnegie Mellon University Professors

The courses are designed by Carnegie Mellon University professors of engineering.

This provides learners with access to structured educational content developed within one of the world’s recognised technology and engineering-focused university environments.

The program combines this academic foundation with hands-on learning and current AI tools, frameworks, and practices.

Important Things Applicants Should Know

Before applying, prospective learners should understand the following:

  1. The program is online.
  2. It consists of six courses.
  3. The certificate program is cost-free for qualified applicants.
  4. It is not university credit.
  5. Learners earn digital badges for individual courses.
  6. A shareable and verifiable certificate is awarded after completing all six courses.
  7. Learners should plan for approximately five to six hours per week.
  8. Each course contains approximately 14–15 lessons.
  9. Each course requires approximately 45 hours to complete at the expected pace.
  10. Applicants need basic knowledge of linear algebra, probability, statistics, and programming.
  11. Applicants need a laptop or desktop computer.
  12. Applicants need a reliable internet connection.
  13. Applications and recommendations open on 15 October 2026.
  14. Applications and recommendations close on 15 November 2026.
  15. The new cohort begins on 17 January 2027.

Official Program Information

For complete and current information about the program, eligibility requirements, application process, and timeline, applicants should consult the official Carnegie Mellon University Africa website.

Carnegie Mellon University Africa – Certificate in Artificial Intelligence for Africa

Questions about the certificate can also be directed to the program team at cmuafricacerts@andrew.cmu.edu.

Click HERE to read more and apply.

Conclusion

The Carnegie Mellon University Africa Certificate in Artificial Intelligence for Africa offers qualified learners an opportunity to develop practical AI knowledge through a structured six-course online program.

The curriculum combines AI context and technical training, covering artificial intelligence, machine learning in Africa, Python for AI, mathematical foundations of machine learning, machine learning essentials, and applied generative AI.

The program is particularly relevant for undergraduate students, early-career learners, and professionals who want to strengthen their technical capabilities and explore career pathways connected to artificial intelligence.

Importantly, the certificate program is cost-free for qualified applicants, although participants must have the required foundational knowledge, computer access, and reliable internet connection.

Applications and recommendations open on 15 October 2026 and close on 15 November 2026, with the new cohort beginning on 17 January 2027.

For learners interested in developing AI capabilities while exploring how artificial intelligence can be applied to African contexts, this program provides a structured opportunity to build foundational and practical skills.

Click HERE for more short courses.
