item.content:encoded:
YLabs is accepting applications for an Operations Specialist to join its growing People Operations function. The position is a full-time, remote opportunity that can be performed from anywhere in Africa and is particularly suitable for professionals with experience in operations, human resources, recruitment, administration, employee experience, or people operations.

The successful candidate will play a central role in ensuring that the practical systems behind YLabs’ globally distributed workforce operate effectively. The position combines human resources administration, recruitment coordination, onboarding and offboarding, HR information systems, employee experience, vendor management, equipment administration, software access, compliance documentation, and organizational process improvement.

YLabs is looking for a professional who does more than maintain existing systems. The organization wants someone who can identify gaps, improve processes, take ownership of problems, and build operational systems that become more effective as the organization grows. YLabs

The position offers an annual salary range of USD $17,000 to $26,000, depending on experience, with compensation benchmarked for a mid-level P3 position in YLabs Africa. Salaries for full-time employees are paid in the local currency of the employee’s permanent work location. YLabs

About YLabs

YLabs is a global design and research organization that develops technologies, products, and services intended to expand the power, agency, and opportunities available to young people.

According to the organization, YLabs was founded at the Harvard Innovation Lab and works directly with young people to co-create inclusive digital solutions that respond to challenges affecting their lives. Its approach is based on giving young people an active role in designing solutions rather than treating them only as beneficiaries of programs. YLabs

YLabs brings together expertise across several disciplines, including:

  • Youth-driven design
  • Adolescent health
  • Climate resilience
  • Livelihoods
  • Digital product design
  • Behavioral science
  • Epidemiology

YLabs operates with teams in Rwanda and the United States and states that it has worked across 18 countries. Its work is organized around three broad areas: improving health and wellbeing, expanding economic opportunities, and strengthening climate resilience. YLabs

This international and multidisciplinary environment means that the Operations Specialist will support colleagues working across different locations, functions, projects, and cultural contexts.

About the YLabs Operations Specialist Role

YLabs is expanding both its People Operations department and its wider organizational infrastructure.

The Operations Specialist will be responsible for helping create and operate the systems that allow employees to work effectively across a distributed organization.

The vacancy is described as a highly hands-on role. The successful candidate will not simply monitor systems designed by other people; they will be expected to actively identify what is missing, diagnose problems, develop practical solutions, and take initiatives from concept through implementation. YLabs

The position is particularly suitable for professionals currently working as:

  • Operations Specialists
  • Senior Operations Associates
  • People Operations professionals
  • HR Operations professionals
  • Administrative or organizational operations specialists

YLabs specifically notes that applicants do not need previous experience leading an entire People Operations function.

Instead, the organization places considerable emphasis on a candidate’s ability to:

  • Learn quickly
  • Take ownership
  • Build trust
  • Exercise sound judgment
  • Improve systems
  • Execute reliably
  • Complete assignments independently

This makes the opportunity especially relevant to mid-career professionals who have developed solid operational experience and are now ready to assume greater responsibility. YLabs

Main Responsibilities of the Operations Specialist

The Operations Specialist will have responsibilities across several different areas of people and organizational operations.

1. Managing Day-to-Day People Operations

A major component of the position involves managing the practical employee experience at YLabs.

The successful candidate will handle areas such as:

  • Employee onboarding
  • Employee offboarding
  • Staff requests
  • Benefits administration
  • Personnel records
  • General People Operations requirements
  • Internal administrative support

The goal is not merely to process requests but to continually improve how employees experience these systems.

YLabs wants the Operations Specialist to help make internal processes simpler, more responsive, more consistent, and more human. YLabs

2. Managing Recruitment Processes

Recruitment is another significant part of the position.

The Operations Specialist will manage recruitment execution for individual-contributor and coordinator-level vacancies.

Responsibilities may include:

  • Candidate sourcing
  • Initial screening
  • Interview coordination
  • Candidate communications
  • Recruitment administration
  • Offer logistics
  • Managing hiring timelines
  • Maintaining candidate experience

The successful candidate will therefore require both organizational discipline and strong communication skills.

YLabs emphasizes creating a positive recruitment experience for applicants, meaning the Operations Specialist will represent the organization throughout multiple stages of the hiring process. YLabs

Building People Operations Systems as YLabs Grows

This is not designed as a purely administrative position.

A major expectation is that the Operations Specialist will actively help build systems that allow YLabs to scale.

The appointed candidate may be required to:

  • Develop new onboarding procedures
  • Improve equipment-management systems
  • Simplify internal staff-request processes
  • Strengthen HRIS practices
  • Develop new workflows where no effective process currently exists
  • Improve documentation
  • Standardize recurring operations
  • Reduce inefficiencies
  • Develop tools that make employee processes easier to use

YLabs describes the ideal candidate as someone who naturally identifies gaps and begins thinking about how to solve them.

The organization therefore values initiative and process-improvement capability just as highly as the ability to execute existing procedures. YLabs

Taking Ownership of Operational Problems

YLabs expects the Operations Specialist to work independently.

The successful candidate should not require detailed instructions for every assignment.

Instead, they should be comfortable:

  • Identifying a problem
  • Determining the necessary actions
  • Bringing in relevant colleagues when required
  • Making appropriate decisions
  • Escalating issues when necessary
  • Following initiatives through to completion

The position therefore requires a strong sense of personal accountability.

YLabs is specifically looking for someone who takes responsibility for “closing loops,” meaning that assignments, requests, problems, and processes should not remain unresolved because follow-up was overlooked. YLabs

Supporting Employee Experience and Organizational Culture

The Operations Specialist will also contribute to the overall employee experience within YLabs.

Responsibilities include building relationships with employees across the distributed team and understanding what staff need in order to work effectively.

The role may involve:

  • Supporting staff wellness
  • Improving team connection
  • Organizing staff events
  • Helping coordinate YLabs’ annual retreat
  • Reviewing employee feedback
  • Using pulse survey data
  • Identifying opportunities to improve workplace systems
  • Strengthening communication and internal processes

This aspect of the position means that interpersonal skills are particularly important.

The successful candidate must be able to balance operational efficiency with empathy, discretion, and sensitivity to the employee experience. YLabs

Managing Technology, Equipment, Vendors and Internal Systems

The Operations Specialist will also manage several practical systems required by a distributed organization.

These responsibilities can include:

  • Google Workspace administration
  • Access to software platforms
  • Equipment administration
  • Supplies
  • Vendor management
  • Contract administration
  • Operational documentation
  • Compliance records

Because YLabs operates as a geographically distributed organization, these systems must remain organized, accessible, reliable, and well documented.

The Operations Specialist will also be expected to identify opportunities to improve their efficiency and usability rather than simply maintaining the status quo. YLabs

Working with the Deputy Director of People Operations

The successful candidate will work closely with YLabs’ Deputy Director, People Operations.

This partnership will involve translating broader People Operations priorities into practical day-to-day implementation.

The Operations Specialist will be expected to:

  • Communicate operational issues early
  • Identify emerging problems
  • Surface improvement opportunities
  • Help implement People Operations priorities
  • Provide insight into employees’ day-to-day operational experience
  • Convert strategic ideas into practical processes

YLabs also indicates that the position may expand over time, giving the successful candidate opportunities to assume additional ownership as the organization grows. YLabs

Essential Qualifications and Experience

Applicants should carefully evaluate their experience against the requirements published by YLabs.

Professional Experience

Candidates should have approximately:

3–6 years of professional experience

in one or more of the following fields:

  • Operations
  • People Operations
  • Human Resources
  • Administration
  • Related operational functions

Experience in an NGO, research institution, social-impact organization, or distributed/multi-country organization is considered beneficial. YLabs

Strong Organizational and Execution Skills

Applicants should be highly organized and capable of managing several responsibilities simultaneously.

YLabs is looking for someone who:

  • Maintains control of multiple priorities
  • Meets commitments
  • Follows through consistently
  • Can work without constant supervision
  • Takes responsibility for completing tasks

The position requires someone who can independently organize their workload while ensuring important details are not overlooked. YLabs

A Builder’s Mindset

One of the most important qualities YLabs emphasizes is what it describes as a builder’s mindset.

The successful candidate should be someone who notices inefficiencies or missing systems and wants to improve them.

This includes being comfortable in an organization where some procedures may still be evolving.

Candidates who prefer highly rigid environments where every process is already fully documented may find this type of position more challenging.

YLabs instead wants someone who can operate effectively in ambiguity and help create structure where necessary. YLabs

People-Centered Judgment and Discretion

Because the Operations Specialist will handle employee information, recruitment processes, personnel matters, and potentially sensitive issues, strong professional judgment is essential.

Applicants should demonstrate:

  • Empathy
  • Discretion
  • Professional maturity
  • Strong relationship-building ability
  • Thoughtful communication
  • Ability to manage sensitive situations appropriately

This combination of operational capability and interpersonal judgment is central to the role. YLabs

Recruitment Experience

Applicants should have experience supporting or managing recruitment activities.

This should include familiarity with areas such as:

  • Candidate sourcing
  • Screening
  • Interview scheduling
  • Candidate correspondence
  • Hiring coordination
  • Offer administration

Professionals who have already worked in HR recruitment operations or talent coordination may therefore be particularly well suited to this requirement. YLabs

Communication Skills

Strong written and verbal communication skills are required.

Because the successful applicant will interact with employees, candidates, managers, vendors, and other stakeholders, they must be able to communicate clearly and professionally across different situations.

Strong communication is particularly important in a remote and multi-country working environment where employees may rely heavily on digital collaboration. YLabs

Autonomy, Initiative and Problem Solving

Candidates should be comfortable working independently.

YLabs wants someone who can determine when they have enough information to make a decision and when an issue requires escalation or additional guidance.

Applicants should also demonstrate:

  • Curiosity
  • Initiative
  • Creativity in problem solving
  • Willingness to question inefficient practices
  • Ability to experiment with new solutions

This emphasis makes the position particularly attractive for operations professionals who want meaningful ownership rather than a narrowly defined administrative role. YLabs

Desirable Qualifications

In addition to the essential requirements, YLabs lists several areas of experience that would strengthen an application.

These include:

  • Experience supporting distributed teams
  • Experience working across multiple countries
  • Experience managing vendors
  • Experience managing contracts
  • Familiarity with HR information systems
  • Experience using BambooHR or similar platforms
  • Experience working in a growing organization
  • Experience building or improving processes in environments where systems are still evolving

These qualifications are described as desirable rather than mandatory. YLabs

Is a University Degree Required?

The official vacancy does not specify a mandatory bachelor’s or master’s degree.

Instead, YLabs focuses its published requirements on relevant professional experience, operational capability, recruitment knowledge, judgment, communication, initiative, and systems-building ability. YLabs

Applicants should therefore evaluate themselves primarily against the stated experience and competency requirements rather than assuming that a particular academic qualification is necessary.

Job Location: Remote Across Africa

The Operations Specialist position is remote and can be based anywhere in Africa.

This is one of the most important eligibility conditions.

Applicants do not appear to be restricted to Rwanda or another specific African country, provided their permanent work location is within Africa. YLabs

The position may occasionally require travel for:

  • Meetings
  • Team gatherings
  • Off-sites
  • Other organizational activities

YLabs states that it will fully reimburse required travel. YLabs

Job Type and Expected Start Date

The Operations Specialist vacancy is a:

Full-time position

The anticipated start date is:

October 2026. YLabs

Because applications are being considered on a rolling basis, candidates interested in starting within this timeframe should apply as early as possible.

YLabs Operations Specialist Salary

The published annual salary range is:

USD $17,000–$26,000 per year

Final compensation will depend on the applicant’s experience.

YLabs categorizes the role as a P3 mid-level position within its Africa compensation framework. YLabs

The organization states that the salary range has been benchmarked regionally.

Full-time staff are paid in the local currency of their permanent work location rather than necessarily receiving their salary directly in U.S. dollars. YLabs

YLabs Compensation Philosophy

YLabs states that its approach to compensation follows principles associated with Project Fair and the concept of equal pay for work of equal value.

Salary ranges are determined according to the employee’s organizational level and benchmarked against relevant regional and national labor markets. YLabs

This is particularly relevant in a geographically distributed organization because employees may work from countries with substantially different labor-market conditions.

Application Deadline

YLabs has not published a fixed final deadline for this vacancy.

Instead:

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled. YLabs

This means the vacancy may close once YLabs identifies and hires a suitable candidate.

Applicants should therefore avoid waiting for a traditional closing date.

How the Application Process Works

YLabs states that every application will be reviewed carefully.

Due to the expected volume of applications, however, only candidates whose qualifications most closely match the requirements may be contacted to discuss the next stage of the recruitment process. YLabs

Candidates should therefore make sure their application clearly demonstrates:

  1. Their 3–6 years of relevant experience.
  2. Their operations or People Operations background.
  3. Recruitment experience.
  4. Examples of systems or processes they have built or improved.
  5. Experience working independently.
  6. Experience handling several priorities simultaneously.
  7. Employee or stakeholder relationship-management skills.
  8. Experience with HRIS platforms, if applicable.
  9. Experience supporting remote or distributed teams.
  10. Vendor or contract management experience, if applicable.

Because YLabs places substantial emphasis on ownership and problem solving, candidates should provide examples of situations where they independently identified and resolved operational problems.

Background Checks

Any employment offer issued by YLabs is conditional on satisfactory:

  • Background checks
  • Criminal record clearances

The organization also states that applicant information will be handled confidentially in accordance with applicable equal-employment-opportunity guidelines. YLabs

Equal Employment Opportunity at YLabs

YLabs explicitly states its commitment to equity, justice, and belonging within its workforce.

The organization encourages applicants from diverse:

  • Cultures
  • Races
  • Educational backgrounds
  • Socioeconomic backgrounds
  • Sexual orientations
  • Age groups
  • Genders
  • Physical abilities

YLabs also states that it does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, familial status, marital status, caregiver status, or other legally protected characteristics. YLabs

Why This Operations Specialist Opportunity Stands Out

The YLabs Operations Specialist vacancy differs from many conventional administrative positions because of its broad ownership and systems-building responsibilities.

The successful applicant will not merely execute predefined HR procedures.

Instead, the position combines:

  • People Operations
  • Recruitment
  • Employee experience
  • HR systems
  • Process design
  • Technology administration
  • Vendor management
  • Organizational operations
  • Compliance administration
  • Employee engagement
  • Continuous improvement

This breadth can make the position particularly valuable for mid-career operations professionals seeking to move toward more senior People Operations or organizational leadership positions.

Who Is Most Likely to Be Competitive?

A particularly strong candidate would likely be someone with approximately three to six years of experience who has already worked across several areas of HR or operations rather than exclusively within one narrow administrative function.

Competitive candidates may have experience in environments such as:

  • International NGOs
  • Research organizations
  • Social enterprises
  • Development organizations
  • Remote-first companies
  • International nonprofit organizations
  • Growing startups
  • Multi-country teams

Candidates who can demonstrate that they have personally improved systems, managed recruitment workflows, supported employees, coordinated vendors, and solved operational problems independently may be particularly well aligned with the vacancy.

Tips for Preparing a Strong Application

Applicants should tailor their CV specifically to the role rather than submitting a generic operations resume.

Strong applications should highlight measurable examples.

For example, candidates may wish to demonstrate:

  • Number of employees supported
  • Number of recruitments coordinated
  • Number of countries supported
  • Improvements made to onboarding timelines
  • Employee-service improvements
  • Systems implemented
  • Administrative costs reduced
  • HRIS improvements
  • Vendor contracts managed
  • Equipment systems developed
  • Employee engagement initiatives coordinated

Specific evidence is generally more persuasive than simply stating that an applicant has “strong operations experience.”

Applicants should also review their CV for examples demonstrating ownership, initiative, and independent judgment because these qualities appear repeatedly throughout YLabs’ official description of the position. YLabs

Conclusion

The YLabs Operations Specialist 2026 opportunity offers experienced African operations and People Operations professionals the chance to join an international organization working at the intersection of youth, design, technology, research, health, economic opportunity, and climate resilience.

The position is full-time and remotely based anywhere in Africa, with an annual salary range of USD $17,000 to $26,000, benchmarked according to YLabs’ Africa compensation framework. YLabs

Successful applicants will take responsibility for employee operations, recruitment, onboarding and offboarding, HR systems, vendors, technology access, employee experience, process improvement, and operational infrastructure.

Candidates should normally have 3–6 years of relevant professional experience, strong organizational and communication skills, recruitment experience, sound professional judgment, and an ability to build and improve systems independently. YLabs

No fixed application deadline is currently published. Applications are being reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled, making early submission advisable. YLabs

item.content:encoded:
The Canada Graduate Research Scholarship – Doctoral (CGRS D) Program provides substantial financial support to outstanding doctoral students conducting research in health, natural sciences and engineering, social sciences and humanities. The scholarship is jointly administered through Canada’s three federal research agencies: the Canadian Institutes of Health Research (CIHR), the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC), and the Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC).

Successful scholars receive $40,000 per year for three years, allowing them to devote greater attention to doctoral research, work with leading research mentors and contribute to Canada’s research and innovation ecosystem.

The program also supports interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary research and includes priority research areas such as artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, health, climate resilience, food and water security, democratic and community resilience, advanced manufacturing, and defence-related technologies.

Opportunity Details

  • Opportunity: Canada Graduate Research Scholarship – Doctoral (CGRS D)
  • Category: Scholarship
  • Study level: Doctoral / PhD
  • Funding: $40,000 per year
  • Duration: 36 months
  • Application deadline: October 17, 2026, for applicants applying directly to an agency
  • Institutional deadline: Varies by Canadian institution and may be significantly earlier
  • Fields: Health, natural sciences, engineering, social sciences and humanities
  • Eligible applicants: Canadian and eligible international doctoral students
  • Study location: Eligible Canadian institutions and, under specific conditions, eligible degree-granting institutions outside Canada
  • Administered by: CIHR, NSERC and SSHRC

About the Canada Graduate Research Scholarship – Doctoral Program

The CGRS D is part of Canada’s Canada Research Training Awards Suite (CRTAS).

The broader suite includes:

  1. Canada Graduate Research Scholarship – Master’s (CGRS M)
  2. Canada Graduate Research Scholarship – Doctoral (CGRS D)
  3. Canada Postdoctoral Research Award (CPRA)

The CGRS D is designed to recognize and support outstanding doctoral researchers and help develop the next generation of highly qualified innovators, knowledge workers and creative thinkers.

The scholarship provides recipients with financial support that can enable them to concentrate more fully on their doctoral studies and research activities. It also provides flexibility for scholars to seek strong research mentors and participate in Canada’s research ecosystem.

The program covers a broad range of academic disciplines, including research in:

  • Health
  • Natural sciences
  • Engineering
  • Social sciences
  • Humanities
  • Interdisciplinary research
  • Multidisciplinary research

Scholarship Value and Duration

Successful CGRS D recipients receive:

$40,000 per year for 36 months.

This represents a total potential scholarship value of:

$120,000 over three years.

The funding is intended to support doctoral students while they undertake eligible research-oriented doctoral studies.

The financial support can allow recipients to dedicate more time to their research, develop their research skills, work with appropriate research mentors and contribute to research activities during and after the scholarship period.

Who Can Apply?

The CGRS D is intended for outstanding doctoral students who are undertaking eligible research-oriented doctoral programs.

Applicants must satisfy the program’s eligibility requirements, including requirements relating to their doctoral study progress and registration status.

Doctoral Study Requirement

By December 31 of the calendar year of application, applicants must have completed no more than 36 months of full-time equivalent study in the doctoral program for which they are requesting funding.

The calculation includes the applicable doctoral studies regardless of whether those studies were completed at the same institution or within the same program.

The agencies count:

  • All months of full-time study, including summer months
  • Two terms of part-time study as one term of full-time study
  • Previous doctoral study toward the same degree, even if completed at another institution or in another program

Fast-Track Programs

For applicants who transferred from a master’s program into a doctoral program through a fast-track arrangement, the months of study are calculated beginning from the date of transfer into the doctoral program.

Joint Programs

For joint programs such as:

  • MA/PhD
  • MSc/PhD
  • MBA/PhD

the calculation begins from the date the applicant officially registered in either portion of the joint program, including the master’s portion.

Joint Professional Undergraduate/PhD Programs

For programs such as:

  • MD/PhD
  • JD/PhD
  • DVM/PhD

only the months completed in the PhD portion are counted.

Requirements for the Doctoral Program

The doctoral program must be predominantly research-oriented.

It must lead to a substantial research or scholarly requirement such as:

  • A thesis
  • A dissertation
  • A major research project
  • Scholarly publication
  • Performance
  • Recital
  • Exhibit

The research or scholarly work must be subject to merit review by a panel of experts at the institution as part of the requirements for completing the program.

Certain joint professional doctoral programs can also qualify when they contain a significant autonomous research component.

This includes eligible joint programs involving professional degrees such as:

  • MD/PhD
  • DVM/PhD
  • JD/PhD
  • MBA/PhD

Clinically oriented programs can also qualify when they meet the program’s research requirements. Clinical psychology is specifically mentioned as an example.

International Applicants

International students can apply, but specific conditions apply.

If you are not a Canadian citizen, permanent resident of Canada or protected person under Canada’s Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, you must be registered in your doctoral program at an eligible Canadian institution by the application deadline.

The program states that up to 15% of awards will be available to international applicants.

This is particularly important for international students considering the opportunity from outside Canada: simply being an international student is not enough. The applicant must meet the doctoral registration requirement at an eligible Canadian institution by the relevant deadline.

Can the Scholarship Be Held Outside Canada?

The CGRS D may be held at an eligible Canadian institution or, under certain conditions, at a degree-granting institution outside Canada.

However, holding the scholarship outside Canada is subject to additional eligibility requirements.

To hold the award at an eligible degree-granting institution outside Canada, an applicant must:

  • Be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident of Canada or protected person as of the application deadline; and
  • Have completed at least one previous undergraduate or graduate degree at a Canadian institution.

The program indicates that up to 20% of all doctoral awards may be available to be held outside Canada.

Therefore, the rules for holding the award outside Canada are different from the rules governing international applicants who are studying in Canada.

Important Application Restrictions

Applicants should carefully review the restrictions before applying.

One CRTAS Application Per Academic Year

Applicants can apply to only one CRTAS program per academic year through CIHR, NSERC or SSHRC.

If an applicant submits applications to more than one program, only the first eligible application submitted to the agencies will be retained.

Maximum of Three CGRS D Applications

An individual can apply to the CGRS D program a maximum of three times.

Previous Doctoral Scholarships

Applicants cannot have already received a doctoral-level scholarship from CIHR, NSERC or SSHRC.

This includes the Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarship.

Tenure or Tenure-Track Positions

Additional restrictions apply to applicants who hold tenure or tenure-track appointments.

Recipients of CIHR or NSERC awards cannot simultaneously hold a tenure or tenure-track appointment or be on leave from such an appointment during their CGRS D award.

SSHRC has different provisions for approved leave from a tenure or tenure-track position when undertaking a first doctoral degree.

Applicants who are uncertain about their eligibility should contact the relevant agency.

Priority Research Areas

The Government of Canada has identified several priority research areas that may receive additional award offers for meritorious applications aligned with these areas.

These include:

1. Advanced Digital Technologies

Research may include areas such as:

  • Artificial intelligence
  • Quantum technologies
  • Cybersecurity
  • Other advanced digital technologies

2. Health and Biotechnology

This includes research connected to:

  • Health
  • Biotechnology
  • Related scientific and medical research areas

3. Clean Technology and Resource Value Chains

Research addressing clean technologies and sustainable resource-related systems may align with this priority.

4. Environment, Climate Resilience and the Arctic

Research related to environmental challenges, climate resilience and Arctic issues is included among the priority areas.

5. Food and Water Security

Research addressing food systems, water security and related global challenges may align with this area.

6. Democratic and Community Resilience

Research examining issues related to democratic systems and community resilience is another identified priority.

7. Manufacturing and Advanced Materials

This includes research involving advanced manufacturing and materials science.

8. Defence and Dual-Use Technologies

Research related to defence and technologies with potential civilian and defence applications is also included.

Applicants whose research aligns with a priority area should consult the relevant agency’s application instructions for guidance on identifying that alignment.

Additional Funding Opportunities

CGRS D recipients may also be eligible for supplementary funding.

The three agencies may offer joint initiatives and supplements in collaboration with organizations from:

  • The public sector
  • Private sector
  • Not-for-profit sector

These initiatives can support research training, networking and other activities connected with the strategic objectives of the participating organizations.

Additional funding opportunities may vary by agency and competition.

Support for Indigenous Student Researchers

The program includes specific measures supporting Indigenous student researchers and Indigenous research.

The Indigenous Scholars Awards and Supplements Pilot Initiative can provide additional support to eligible Indigenous students whose nations or communities are located in Canada.

Successful eligible CGRS D applicants may receive an Indigenous Scholars Supplement valued at $5,000 for one year, subject to available funding and the relevant conditions.

The program also includes measures designed to support Indigenous research and respectful relationships with Indigenous Peoples and communities.

These measures include provisions concerning:

  • Indigenous research
  • Self-identified Indigenous doctoral applicants
  • Research review
  • Special circumstances affecting academic or career paths
  • Indigenous representation and expertise on review committees

Additional Support for Black Student Researchers

The Government of Canada has also provided additional funding intended to increase direct support for Black student researchers.

Meritorious CGRS D applicants who self-identify as Black and consent to being considered for designated funding may be selected for this additional support.

Each of the three agencies may have up to 10 additional awards reserved for Black student researchers.

These opportunities are subject to the program’s eligibility, selection and funding conditions.

How to Apply

Applicants must apply through the agency that is best aligned with the subject matter of their proposed research.

The three relevant agencies are:

  • CIHR – Canadian Institutes of Health Research
  • NSERC – Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada
  • SSHRC – Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council

Selecting the correct agency is important because applications are reviewed by experts whose disciplinary expertise should correspond to the applicant’s field of research.

CIHR Applicants

Applicants applying through CIHR should use the ResearchNET platform and follow CIHR’s specific application instructions.

NSERC Applicants

Applicants applying through NSERC should use NSERC’s online application system and follow the CGRS D application instructions.

SSHRC Applicants

Applicants applying through SSHRC should use the SSHRC registration and application system and follow the agency’s specific doctoral scholarship instructions.

Applicants who are uncertain about which agency is appropriate should review the federal guidance on selecting the appropriate granting agency or contact the relevant agency.

Where Should Applicants Submit Their Applications?

The correct application channel depends on the applicant’s registration status and, in some cases, whether the institution has a doctoral award quota.

Submitting through the wrong channel can result in rejection.

International Applicants

International applicants have specific submission rules.

An international applicant who is currently registered in a doctoral program at a Canadian institution with a doctoral award quota for the relevant agency generally applies through that Canadian institution.

An international applicant who is registered in a doctoral program at a Canadian institution without a doctoral award quota for the selected agency applies directly to the appropriate agency.

Applicants on an approved leave of absence from an institution are considered to remain registered at that institution for these purposes.

Canadian Applicants

For Canadian citizens, permanent residents and protected persons, the submission route depends on their registration status during the calendar year of application and the institution involved.

Depending on the circumstances, an applicant may need to apply:

  • Through their current Canadian institution
  • Through a Canadian institution where they were registered during the year
  • Directly to the relevant federal agency

Applicants should carefully review the official submission tables and confirm their status with their faculty of graduate studies or equivalent office where necessary.

Understanding Institutional Quotas

A quota refers to the maximum number of applications that a Canadian institution can forward to a particular federal research agency.

Institutions have separate quotas for:

  • CIHR
  • NSERC
  • SSHRC

If an applicant must apply through an institution, they should contact the relevant graduate studies office to determine:

  • Whether the institution has a quota
  • Which agency’s quota applies
  • The institution’s internal deadline
  • Any internal selection process
  • Required institutional documents

Application Deadline

October 17, 2026

Applicants who are eligible to apply directly to an agency must submit their application before 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time on October 17, 2026.

If the deadline falls on a weekend, applications can be submitted on the following business day before 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time.

Applicants should not wait until the final hours because the agencies warn that high traffic on online application systems can cause delays.

Institutional Deadlines

Applicants applying through a Canadian institution must follow the institution’s own deadline.

The institutional deadline can be significantly earlier than October 17.

Therefore, applicants should contact their university’s faculty of graduate studies as early as possible rather than relying solely on the federal agency deadline.

Late applications are not accepted.

What Happens After Submission?

Applications undergo an evaluation process.

Institutional Review

Where applications are submitted through a Canadian institution, the institution’s faculty of graduate studies or equivalent body coordinates an institutional evaluation.

The institution then forwards applications according to its available agency quota.

Agency Review

Applications submitted directly to an agency, as well as applications forwarded by Canadian institutions, are evaluated by agency-specific review committees.

The reviewers assess the applications according to the CGRS D selection criteria.

How Applications Are Evaluated

The CGRS D uses two major selection criteria.

1. Research Potential – 50%

Research potential accounts for 50% of the assessment.

Reviewers consider factors including:

  • Quality of the research proposal
  • Specificity and focus of the research question or objectives
  • Feasibility of the proposed research
  • Quality of the methodology
  • Significance of the proposed research
  • Expected contribution to the relevant research field
  • Potential to successfully conduct the proposed research
  • Publications and other research outputs
  • Reports
  • Posters
  • Abstracts
  • Presentations
  • Patents
  • Scholarly and creative outputs
  • Knowledge translation activities
  • Community products
  • Critical thinking
  • Sound judgment
  • Originality
  • Initiative
  • Autonomy
  • Community involvement
  • Outreach
  • Responsible and ethical research conduct
  • Ability to communicate research concepts clearly
  • Overall quality and presentation of the application

Where relevant, applicants can also demonstrate how equity, diversity and inclusion considerations are integrated into their research.

2. Relevant Experience and Achievements – 50%

The second half of the assessment focuses on relevant experience and achievements obtained both inside and outside academia.

This criterion accounts for another 50%.

Relevant factors can include:

  • Academic training
  • Relevant professional training
  • Lived experience
  • Traditional teachings
  • Scholarships
  • Awards
  • Academic distinctions
  • Academic record
  • Transcripts
  • Duration of previous studies
  • Courses completed
  • Course load
  • Relative academic standing where available
  • Professional activities
  • Academic activities
  • Extracurricular activities
  • Collaboration with supervisors
  • Collaboration with colleagues and peers
  • Teaching
  • Mentoring
  • Supervision
  • Coaching
  • Project management
  • Science or research promotion
  • Community outreach
  • Volunteer work
  • Civic engagement
  • Committee leadership
  • Conference organization
  • Meeting organization
  • Participation in academic or professional organizations, associations and clubs

This means the application is not assessed solely on the proposed research project. The applicant’s broader academic, professional and extracurricular record is also considered.

Notification of Results

Applicants will be notified of the results by:

April 30.

Successful award holders who accept the scholarship may have their names and basic award information published on the relevant agency’s website.

The agencies’ publication of award information is subject to applicable Canadian privacy and access-to-information legislation.

Official Language of the Application

Applicants can submit their application in either of Canada’s two official languages:

  • English
  • French

If supporting documents are written in a language other than English or French, applicants must provide a certified translation.

Canadian institutions must have mechanisms for reviewing applications in the official language in which they are submitted.

Career Development and Individual Development Plans

The agencies encourage applicants and award holders to actively plan their careers during their research training.

Individual Development Plans, or IDPs, can help doctoral researchers:

  • Identify career objectives
  • Identify skills gaps
  • Develop professional skills
  • Plan career development
  • Reflect on strengths and values
  • Prepare for future employment and research opportunities

However, the program explicitly states that IDPs are not a selection or evaluation criterion for the CGRS D.

Research Security and International Research

Applicants and award holders undertaking research activities outside Canada are encouraged to consult Canadian government resources concerning travel and research security.

Relevant resources include:

  • Travel advice and advisories
  • Travel health notices
  • Registration of Canadians abroad
  • Emergency assistance outside Canada
  • Safeguarding Your Research
  • Research security training resources
  • Guidance concerning research organizations and sensitive technologies

The program also notes that the Policy on Sensitive Technology Research and Affiliations of Concern (STRAC Policy) does not apply to scholarship and fellowship programs such as the Canada Research Training Awards Suite.

Nevertheless, Canadian researchers are encouraged to follow applicable research-security guidance and exercise due diligence when conducting research activities.

Important Things Applicants Should Know

Before applying, prospective applicants should carefully verify the following:

  1. Whether they are eligible for the CGRS D.
  2. How many months of doctoral study they will have completed by December 31.
  3. Whether they have previously received a doctoral-level scholarship from CIHR, NSERC or SSHRC.
  4. Whether they have already applied to another CRTAS program during the academic year.
  5. Whether they have previously applied to the CGRS D and how many applications they have made.
  6. Which federal agency best matches their research subject.
  7. Whether their Canadian institution has an applicable doctoral award quota.
  8. Whether they need to submit through their institution or directly to the agency.
  9. Their institution’s internal deadline.
  10. Whether their doctoral program meets the research-oriented program requirements.
  11. Whether they meet the special registration requirements applicable to international applicants.
  12. Whether all required supporting documents and reference letters will be submitted on time.

Applicants should also avoid waiting until the final day because online application systems may experience heavy traffic near the deadline.

Category of the Opportunity

Scholarship

This is a doctoral research scholarship under Canada’s Canada Research Training Awards Suite.

Who Qualifies for This Opportunity?

The opportunity is primarily for:

  • Current doctoral/PhD students
  • Students in eligible research-oriented doctoral programs
  • Applicants conducting research in eligible fields
  • Canadian citizens, permanent residents and protected persons who meet the program requirements
  • Eligible international doctoral students who are registered at an eligible Canadian institution by the application deadline
  • Applicants who have completed no more than 36 months of full-time equivalent doctoral study by December 31 of the application year

Academic Qualifications

Applicants must be enrolled in an eligible doctoral program that is predominantly research-oriented and includes an appropriate thesis, dissertation, major research project or equivalent scholarly requirement.

Eligible Fields

Research may fall within:

  • Health
  • Natural sciences
  • Engineering
  • Social sciences
  • Humanities
  • Interdisciplinary research
  • Multidisciplinary research

Countries and Regions

The program is administered by the Government of Canada and is open to eligible applicants internationally, but international applicants face specific Canadian doctoral-registration requirements.

For international applicants, the key requirement is that they must be registered in an eligible doctoral program at an eligible Canadian institution by the application deadline.

Therefore, applicants from Ghana, other African countries, Asia, Europe, the Americas, Oceania and other regions may potentially qualify as international applicants if they satisfy the applicable requirements and are registered in an eligible Canadian doctoral program.

Eligibility is not determined simply by nationality or continent. Applicants must satisfy the program’s academic, doctoral-study, registration and other eligibility requirements.

Application Link

Applicants should use the application platform corresponding to their research agency:

  • CIHR: ResearchNET
  • NSERC: NSERC Online Services
  • SSHRC: SSHRC registration and application system

Applicants should first determine which agency best matches their research subject before starting the application.

Official Website

For the full eligibility requirements, application instructions, agency-specific guidance, deadlines and official updates, visit the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC) official CGRS D funding opportunity page.

For more scholarships visit the OFY Website HERE

 

Conclusion

The Canada Graduate Research Scholarship – Doctoral (CGRS D) is a major Canadian doctoral research funding program providing $40,000 annually for up to 36 months, for a potential total of $120,000.

The scholarship covers a broad range of research areas across health, natural sciences, engineering, social sciences and humanities. It also identifies priority areas including artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, quantum technologies, biotechnology, climate resilience, food and water security, democratic and community resilience, advanced manufacturing, and defence and dual-use technologies.

International students can be considered, but they must pay particular attention to the requirement to be registered in an eligible Canadian doctoral program by the application deadline.

Applicants applying directly to an agency must submit their applications by 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time on October 17, 2026, while applicants applying through Canadian institutions must follow their institution’s earlier internal deadline where applicable.

Because the scholarship evaluates both research potential and relevant experience and achievements, prospective applicants should prepare a strong research proposal while also presenting a comprehensive record of their academic, professional, research, leadership, community and extracurricular achievements.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for Cohort 2 of the METI UniPods AI Innovation Programme, an opportunity designed to support innovators developing early-stage artificial intelligence (AI) and AI-enabled solutions.

What Is the METI UniPods AI Innovation Programme?

The METI UniPods AI Innovation Programme is an innovation and capacity-building programme aimed at supporting early-stage innovators working on artificial intelligence and AI-enabled solutions.

The programme brings together technical learning, entrepreneurship development, mentorship and access to a wider innovation network. Through these components, selected innovators can strengthen both the technology behind their solutions and their understanding of how to develop them into viable products.

The programme is particularly relevant for innovators who already have an early-stage AI solution or are actively developing an AI-enabled product and want additional support to take it further.

Who Is the Programme Looking For?

Cohort 2 is looking for innovators developing early-stage AI and AI-enabled solutions.

Applications can be submitted by:

  • Individual innovators
  • Teams of innovators
  • Developers and technical builders working on AI solutions
  • Innovators developing AI-enabled products
  • Early-stage founders and builders seeking to advance their solutions

Applicants should have a genuine interest in building and improving an AI or AI-enabled solution.

The programme places emphasis on actual development rather than presentation alone. Applicants therefore do not need a pitch deck to demonstrate their interest. The focus is on real ideas, real code and the willingness to build.

Female innovators are especially encouraged to apply.

What Will Selected Innovators Receive?

Selected participants will have access to several forms of technical, entrepreneurial and mentorship support.

1. AI Course from MIT

Participants will have access to an AI course from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT).

This component is intended to strengthen participants’ understanding of artificial intelligence and provide additional learning that can support the development of their solutions.

2. AI Technical Skilling

Selected innovators will receive AI technical skilling designed to help them strengthen their technical capabilities.

For innovators who are already building AI or AI-enabled products, technical development can be important for improving their solutions, addressing technical challenges and advancing their projects.

3. Entrepreneurship Programme

Participants will also gain access to Wadhwani’s 14-week entrepreneurship programme.

The programme covers important areas of entrepreneurship and product development, including:

  • Customer discovery
  • Business modelling
  • Taking products to market
  • Investment readiness

This provides innovators with an opportunity to develop not only their technology but also the business and market understanding required to take a solution beyond the development stage.

4. Technical Mentorship

Participants will have access to technical mentors who can provide guidance as they work on their AI solutions.

Mentorship can be particularly useful for innovators who are facing technical challenges or need additional guidance while developing and refining their products.

5. Access to the timbuktoo Network

Selected innovators will also gain access to the wider timbuktoo network.

Being part of a broader innovation network can provide opportunities for participants to connect with other innovators, ecosystem stakeholders and individuals working across the technology and entrepreneurship space.

6. Opportunity to Attend an In-Person Bootcamp in Addis Ababa

Participants may also have the chance to join an in-person bootcamp in Addis Ababa.

The bootcamp can provide an opportunity for selected innovators to engage directly with other participants, mentors and programme stakeholders while working on their solutions in a collaborative environment.
